summary: Pennington County lookout built 1940 on Flag Mountain by CCC labor; register says removed 1975, cab gone, a stone or concrete base remains; sources disagree on build year and 1951 abandonment.

facts.status_note: Cab gone; part of the base remains. The register gives 1975 as the removal year.

access.note: On Black Hills National Forest land; reached by Forest Service Road 189.2 and a short walk, per a hiking blog and an onX trail page

corrections.proposed: omit: no source gives a total tower height
corrections.why: The sources give a 10-foot stone base and a 14 by 14 foot lookout. 4.3 m is about 14 feet, which matches the cab size, not a tower height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts reports the station completed by November 1940 and firelookout gives 1940; the register gives 1940-1941 and a hiking blog and onX give 1941. The story uses 1940 and notes the later dates.

A Black Hills ATV travel site says it was abandoned in 1951, but the staffing lists in the firelookout page and Forest Lookouts run into the 1960s, and the register gives removal in 1975. The story uses the register's 1975 date.
The firelookout page and Forest Lookouts describe a stone or rock-wall base; the hiking blog and onX describe concrete. The story says the sources disagree.

resolved_conflicts.field: staffing start for William A. Reman
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The firelookout page lists W.A. Reman in 1951; Forest Lookouts reports he began on April 28, 1952. The story gives the newspaper date.

notes_for_editor: The brief height 4.3 m is most likely the 14-foot cab dimension, not a tower height; no total height is in the sources, so the height is omitted and a correction proposed. The register's Removed field gives 1975 but no source describes the removal. The base is described as stone (firelookout, Forest Lookouts) or concrete (blog, onX); the photo credits on the firelookout page (National Archives, USFS) have no image URLs in the text we read, so no photos are added. The 1942-1963 lookout names are from the firelookout page only.
